sources.title: Roberta Metsola: biography and historical offices
sources.findings: Read Parliament’s historical-archives biography: born 18 January 1979 in St Julians; University of Malta legal education and subsequent College of Europe study; European Democrat Students secretary-general 2002–2003; Maltese Permanent Representation 2004–2012 and Catherine Ashton legal adviser 2012–2013. The archive’s MEP list ends at 2022 as it switches to the presidency; this is not loss of her parliamentary seat. Its doctorate wording is not converted into an independently verified research PhD; the main profile uses institution and field without inventing degree equivalence or years.

sources.title: The Presidency: Roberta Metsola’s biography
sources.findings: Read current presidency biography: MEP elections in 2013, 2014, 2019 and 2024; EPP coordination in LIBE during 2017–2020; Frontex rapporteur in 2019; European legal specialisation; active pro-accession student campaigning. It explicitly dates Kyiv travel to 1 April 2022. Its promotional institutional reform outcomes are not used as an independent effectiveness audit. The claim about being only the second person with two presidential terms is not repeated without historical-scope qualification.

sources.title: Female candidates secure all three vacant EP seats, 24 April 2013
sources.findings: Read Malta Independent’s report dated 24 April 2013, 17:53: three women elected to fill EP vacancies, including Metsola Tedesco Triccas for the Nationalist Party replacing Simon Busuttil. The vacancy-election date is not conflated with a later recorded mandate start or with a regular EU-wide election. All three women’s selection means she is one of Malta’s first women MEPs, not uniquely the first. Fine-grained transfer counts are not needed or repeated.

sources.title: Provisional border and coast guard reform agreement, 28 March 2019
sources.findings: Read original 28 March 2019 press-release PDF: provisional agreement between Parliament and Council negotiators; Metsola named rapporteur; planned standing corps of 10,000 by 2027 with phased capacity, rights and data safeguards. Formal committee, plenary and Council approval remained future. She was not Frontex director and the target is not a contemporaneous deployment count. This dated release is not a 2026 audit of actual staffing, returns or rights compliance.

sources.title: Election as first vice-president, 12 November 2020
sources.findings: Read original 12 November 2020 election release: sole nominee by deadline, declared first vice-president by the president, replacing Mairead McGuinness on her move to the Commission. No competitive vote total is invented. It also corroborates prior Maltese representation work, Ashton advisory role, education and 2013/2014/2019 parliamentary elections. Its then-current committee and intergroup positions are not automatically carried into 2026.

sources.title: Roberta Metsola elected president, 18 January 2022
sources.findings: Read election article dated 18 January 2022, despite a different date in its reference identifier and a non-English URL slug. The body is English: 458 votes, 690 ballots, 74 blank/invalid, first round, third woman president and youngest elected at that time. Acting presidency began after Sassoli died on 11 January; formal election is 18 January. Her personal election is by MEPs, not direct election of an EU-wide executive president.

sources.title: Completed visits to Kyiv and Poland, 2 April 2022
sources.findings: Read original 2 April 2022 press-release PDF documenting completed Kyiv visit on the preceding Friday, and Saturday visit to Otwock School in the Warsaw region. It names Zelenskyy, Shmyhal and Stefanchuk among meetings. Presidency biography independently gives 1 April. Publication date is not substituted for Kyiv travel date. The evidence supports diplomatic activity, not delivery of a particular aid amount or military shipment.

sources.title: Metsola’s statement on integrity, independence and accountability, 16 January 2023
sources.findings: Read extracted text of the original 16 January 2023 opening statement, especially pages 1–2. It describes initial agreement with group leaders and planned revolving-door, lobbying, access, financial-declaration and whistleblowing measures after a crisis of confidence. It is not final adoption or an outcome audit. AP’s 12 January contemporary report corroborates the corruption-investigation setting. No personal criminal allegation is inferred against Metsola. Screenshot retrieval hit a JavaScript verification wall; only extracted PDF text, not page pixels, was reviewed.

sources.title: Re-election as president for two and a half years, 16 July 2024
sources.findings: Read 16 July 2024 re-election account: 562 votes; 699 total ballots, including 76 blank or invalid; 61 for the other candidate and 312 needed for majority of valid votes. The 562 figure is not out of 699 valid votes. Presidency covers the first two and a half years of the tenth Parliament, until 2027, with possible later renewal, not an automatic term to 2029. The same article explains election from MEPs and representative/procedural powers. The account’s future press conference is not treated as completed.

sources.title: Armistice Day plenary opening, 11 November 2026
sources.findings: Read official Armistice Day speech dated 11 November 2026, 15:00, Brussels, describing her opening of the plenary and remembrance of wartime victims. The homepage relative label Yesterday is not used to infer a different event date. This is completed official activity; no original video was viewed. Unnecessary biographical claims about other people mentioned in the memorial speech are not imported.

sources.title: OACPS–EU Joint Parliamentary Assembly opening, 9 November 2026
sources.findings: Read official 9 November 2026, 17:00, Brussels opening address to the OACPS–EU Joint Parliamentary Assembly. Multilateral cooperation and fuller Samoa Agreement ratification are aspirations, not proof of ratification or demonstrated benefits. The source establishes an actual address instead of merely a scheduled engagement. Attendee counts and population-impact claims are not adopted as audited results.

portraitReview.unresolved: Commons metadata identifies a press point after EU asylum and migration votes on 10 April 2024; uploaded 21 July 2024 by Κυριλλος, 6000×4000, about 6.57 MB. Its external-source licence review is explicitly still pending. Commons summarises attribution, source URL for partial reproduction, integrity of credits and no circumvention, with exclusions for special conditions and logos. Original image download failed with curl exit 22, 403/HTTP000; no cached pixels. Identity, natural color, sharpness, landscape-to-portrait crop and the specific reuse terms remain unverified.
